The noninstrument-rated pilot's spatial disorientation and subsequent loss of airplane control while maneuvering at low altitude, over water with no visible horizon, in dark night conditions, which resulted in a collision with the water.
The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing and subsequent main landing gear collapse.
The instructor pilot’s delayed action and over application of brakes which resulted in a nose-over.

The flight instructor’s delayed remedial action/lack of supervision. Contributing to the accident was the pilot receiving instructions failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll in gusting wind conditions, which resulted in a ground loop.
